title: Mini-Batch Risk-Averse Deep Q-Learning: A Robot Navigation Case Study
summary: We study the control of Markov decision processes in which the quality of a policy is evaluated by a dynamic, time-consistent Markov risk measure rather than by an expected discounted cost. The main obstacle to combining such measures with reinforcement learning is that a transition risk mapping depends on the transition kernel in a nonlinear way, and therefore cannot be estimated from a single observed transition.
